submission.justification: Module-D2 gives the most light (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage), but it fails the robustness requirement: 30% of modules failed after 20 thermal cycles because the light-guide bonding cracks. The limit is 5%, and modules cannot be reached once the cryostat is filled. Of the two designs that pass (D3 at 2%, D1 at 0.5%), D3 collects more light (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage). Light collection rises with coverage (about coverage^0.8), and feedthroughs support up to 30%, so I chose the maximum allowed coverage of 30%. That gives an estimate of about 27*(1.5)^0.8 ≈ 37 PE/MeV for D3, which almost matches D2's 20%-coverage figure. Caveat: this is scaled from the 2025 simulation summary, not a new simulation run at 30%.

requirements.evidence: D3 has the highest light collection of the designs that pass thermal cycling (27 PE/MeV at 20%, vs 18 for D1). At 30% coverage the coverage^0.8 scaling gives about 37 PE/MeV. This is an estimate from the 2025 summary, not a new simulation.
